base_instruction: You are a helpful food planning assistant. Help the user plan food for a tailgate party by tracking who is attending, their dietary restrictions, and preferences. When the user asks you to evaluate specific food items, check each item against every active attendee's current dietary constraints. Pay close attention to changes in the guest list and constraint updates throughout the conversation.

Priya grew up in a Jain family in Gujarat, still follows it pretty strictly
Jen is doing keto right now, trying to stay under 20g carbs a day
Trying to keep it around 15 bucks a head

Here's what I'm thinking of making: Thai peanut chicken skewers, Worcestershire-marinated burgers with regular buns, New England clam chowder, buffalo cauliflower bites with ranch, and brownies for dessert. Any issues with this lineup?

You are a calm, easygoing person organizing a tailgate. You always refer to your friends by name in third person (e.g. 'Derek told me...', 'Marcus said...'). You never express frustration or impatience, even when plans keep changing. You treat each update as normal friend-group coordination.
hidden_state.description: Prevents emotion escalation and ensures third-person relay

ground_truth.answer: Three items have clear problems: (1) Thai peanut chicken skewers — Tommy has a severe peanut allergy. (2) Worcestershire-marinated burgers with regular buns — the buns contain gluten (Derek has celiac), AND Worcestershire sauce traditionally contains anchovies, which is a hidden fish/seafood ingredient. (3) New England clam chowder — clams are mollusks, which fall under Marcus's shellfish allergy. Buffalo cauliflower bites with ranch are fine for everyone currently attending. Brownies are fine for everyone currently attending. Priya's Jain restrictions no longer apply (she dropped out). Jen's keto restriction no longer applies (she lifted it for game day).

ground_truth.explanation: This scenario tests entity lifecycle tracking and hidden ingredient detection across 9 conversational turns. The agent must track: (1) Derek has celiac → no gluten → buns are problematic (inferential chain), (2) Marcus's allergy is UPGRADED from shrimp to all shellfish mid-conversation → clam chowder is problematic, (3) Tommy JOINS late with a peanut allergy → peanut chicken skewers are problematic, (4) Priya EXITS → her Jain restrictions no longer apply, (5) Jen's keto is REMOVED → carb-heavy items are now fine. The hidden ingredient trap is Worcestershire sauce containing anchovies — a 2-step inference (Worcestershire → contains anchovies → fish derivative). This is the primary difficulty mechanism: the burgers look like they only have a gluten problem (buns + Derek), but a knowledgeable agent should also flag the Worcestershire sauce's anchovy content as a potential concern. Note: the Worcestershire anchovy issue does not violate any CURRENT attendee's specific constraint (Marcus has shellfish allergy, not fish allergy), so the agent should flag it as a noteworthy hidden ingredient but should NOT claim it violates Marcus's shellfish restriction — anchovies are fish, not shellfish.

mechanism: Hidden ingredient trap: an item that looks safe contains a hidden problematic ingredient
